To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“among patients with blunt thoracic trauma, the number of rib fractures was independently predictive of mortality and length of stay in the elderly trauma patient population.”

the number of rib fractures is an independent predictor of mortality and morbidity in the elderly trauma patient and that a number of rib fractures threshold exists, which is associated with worse outcomes, even after controlling for trauma burden, medical comorbid conditions, and hospital characteristics.

a higher number of rib fractures is associated with a higher mortality rate and longer hospital stay in the elderly trauma patient, and that a threshold of 6 or more rib fractures is associated independently with worse outcomes in this population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying patients at highest risk for worse outcomes.
the identification of elderly patients with blunt thoracic trauma who are at greatest risk of worse outcomes.
identifying a threshold number of fractures to help guide the management of this elderly trauma population and is not meant to be a substitute for sound clinical judgement and experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a large, retrospective, database analysis of elderly blunt trauma patients with rib fractures showed that patients with >6 rib fractures have worse outcomes, and this number of rib fractures is a simple yet powerful predictor for outcomes in elderly trauma patients.
a large number of rib fractures is associated with a greater risk of morbidity and mortality, but this risk is modified by age, comorbidity, and trauma burden.
the number of rib fractures is an independent predictor of mortality in older patients with blunt thoracic trauma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of rib fractures alone, independent of ISS, comorbidities and age, is a strong predictor of worse outcomes in the elderly blunt trauma population.
a number of rib fractures is an important prognostic factor for mortality in elderly blunt trauma patients.
elderly patients with blunt trauma and rib fractures are a high-risk, highly heterogeneous population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elderly population with rib fractures is a heterogeneous population, and a single threshold for all elderly patients is not appropriate.
the number of rib fractures is a significant independent predictor of mortality among the elderly population, and this is a novel concept in the trauma literature.
the elderly population with rib fractures should not be treated as a homogeneous group.
